summary: Contrastive GOOD-vs-BAD few-shot on RAG base
hypothesis: Prepending a GOOD-vs-BAD worked example should teach the 3B by contrast what positive-only demos and instruction checklists couldn't — specifically, that demonstrating the exact anti-patterns (restating facts, vague filler, compound asks) alongside a good response might suppress those errors and unlock coverage gains without adding a runtime judging step.
technique: Built on the exp003 RAG positive few-shot base, then prepended one fixed contrastive worked example on a neutral non-eval task ("Organize my garage") whose weak set explicitly demonstrates the anti-patterns the judge flags — restating given facts, off-task questions, vague filler, compound asks, and redundant pairs — paired with a strong counterexample. No extra model calls; the contrast is baked into the prompt.
result: Scored 0.323 on the dev-10 eval (0 wins / 1 tie / 9 losses vs Sonnet), a marginal +0.003 over exp003's 0.320 — within run-to-run noise, treated as a tie. All five rubric dimensions were identical to exp003 (atom 5, spec 3, cover 3, nat 3, nonRed 3), with coverage pinned at 3 and the same per-case misses recurring verbatim. Kept as new best, but the hypothesis is essentially falsified: contrastive negative demonstrations confer no coverage benefit beyond the ~0.32 in-context plateau.
label: exp011
